item.text: {"text":"Relevant 2024–2025 work supports text-enhanced sequential representations, but the retrieved papers do not establish the exact setting of BERT4Rec with a jointly trained, randomly initialized title/description encoder. [The Elephant in the Room (RecSys 2024)](https://github.com/777pomingzi/Rethinking-PLM-in-RS) transfers behavior-tuned language-model embeddings into BERT4Rec; its “from scratch” procedure still starts from pretrained Longformer weights. [DenseRec (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.18442) learns a projection connecting pretrained content embeddings with ID embeddings, reporting gains over ID-only SASRec mainly when histories contain unseen items. These results motivate representation integration, but do not demonstrate gains under the proposed restrictions.\n\n[JEPA4Rec (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.10512) provides related motivation through masked prediction of item-text representations and self-supervised training, though its architecture and training setup differ. A constraint-compatible hypothesis is a small randomly initialized token embedding encoder that pools titles/descriptions, projects them into BERT4Rec’s hidden dimension, and jointly learns their contribution alongside item IDs using masked-item supervision. Use the same combined representation for candidate scoring within one network per category. Remove both ID and text of masked targets to prevent leakage; retain appended-mask inference. Complementary compatibility remains a hypothesis: textual similarity alone does not establish complementarity, and the retrieved studies do not validate that claim for this benchmark. Compare against ID-only BERT4Rec using the fixed macro validation HR@10."}
